A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MentisOculi study. Their complete text, figures, tables and appendices support reliable comparison. Revised task and evaluation settings require care when comparing individual scores.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations on five visual reasoning tasks, diagnostic experiments and a five-participant human study.

after.justification: v2 retains original model and human results and adds model comparisons, fine-tuning controls, oracle-feedback experiments and image/text disagreement analyses.

M1.justification: The benchmark framework is retained, with localized procedural changes. Appendix A revises the Hinge Folding generator's rotation and visibility constraints, and Section 4.3 adapts the existing video action extractor to image-only UMM rollouts.

E1.justification: The same five tasks and human population remain. However, Hinge Folding's task requirements change from 45-degree to 90-degree rotations, while a minimum-visible-area constraint replaces the exclusion of certain 180-degree rotations (Section 2, Appendix A and prompts). This revises one task's generated configurations and action space.

E2.justification: v2 adds evaluated comparisons with Latent Sketchpad, Emu 3.5 and Wan 2.6 (Figures 2–3), plus text-only fine-tuned controls for Mirage and Latent Sketchpad (Table 1). Gemini 3-I also joins the broader task and oracle comparisons where v1 principally evaluated Gemini 2.5-I.

E3.justification: Section 3.2 changes Rush Hour scoring from requiring a successful terminal state to accepting a trace containing a successful state. Appendix G.1 reports increasing Gemini 3-I's retry limit from three to nine and allowing fifteen attempts for Emu 3.5. New protocols include matched text-only fine-tuning controls, iterative oracle feedback and filtered-versus-unfiltered evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds controls testing whether latent gains arise from fine-tuning, whether oracle failures reflect simultaneous multi-image input, and whether excluding image-free responses affects accuracy (Table 1; Figures 14 and 24). It also adds direct image/text solution-disagreement analysis and MLLM oracle experiments (Figures 7 and 15), while expanding existing rollout diagnostics.

E5.justification: Both versions display uncertainty bars or bands and reference 95% confidence intervals in Appendix D.2. No new repeated-run, seed or uncertainty-estimation procedure is reported. Increased retries concern obtaining valid responses rather than estimating statistical uncertainty.

E6.justification: Substantial results are added for new comparators and controls. Table 1 reports Latent Sketchpad's Level 3 accuracy as 6.7% with latents versus 23.3% with text-only training; Table 2 newly reports overall omission rates of 28.9%, 0.9% and 27.2% for Emu 3.5, Gemini 2.5-I and Gemini 3-I. Figures 7 and 15 add modality-disagreement and MLLM oracle findings. Revised Hinge Folding scores concern changed task conditions.

T1.justification: Neither version contains substantive theoretical propositions or proofs. The revisions concern empirical task construction, scoring and analysis rather than new mathematical derivations or formal guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the same central claims: MentisOculi probes multi-step mental imagery, self-generated visuals provide no reliable reasoning advantage, and UMMs struggle with generation consistency and using visual evidence. The added experiments support these retained claims.

C2.justification: v2 develops a stronger interpretation of weak coupling between image and text reasoning, argues that greater model capability does not resolve it, and distinguishes MLLMs' oracle benefits from UMM limitations. New controls qualify the contribution of latent decoding and explanations based on input burden. Conversely, removing v1's datasheet deletes explicit boundaries against interpreting the benchmark as evidence about real-world perception or general intelligence.

D1.justification: Appendix G adds Latent Sketchpad's backbone, LoRA settings, training stages and losses, plus Mirage's text-only training details and model-specific retry information. v1's datasheet guidance on splits, licensing, distribution and maintenance disappears. The Gemini 2.5 endpoint entry changes from gemini-2.5-flash-image to gemini-2.5-flash, but the following sentence still specifies flash-image, leaving the actual configuration ambiguous.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for Latent Sketchpad and Wan 2.6 and removes Gebru et al.'s datasheet reference alongside the datasheet. The broader related-work discussion and benchmark novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section order remain recognizable. Changes include targeted prose corrections, author-year citations, a corrected Form Board prompt heading, added analysis and conflict-of-interest sections, and appendix renumbering after inserting the latent-decoding section and removing the datasheet.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands and restructures the displays: comparator plots gain series, oracle plots use new groupings, and separate rollout diagnostics become multi-model grids. It adds disagreement, iterative-feedback, MLLM-oracle and filtering figures, two tables and Emu examples. Existing human and video figures are largely retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v1 could not isolate latent imagery's contribution from fine-tuning and based its oracle diagnosis mainly on Gemini 2.5-I. v2's text-only training controls, broader oracle comparisons, modality-disagreement analysis and feedback/filtering checks substantially strengthen the central empirical diagnosis. Removing the datasheet loses useful guidance, and inconsistent model descriptions weaken reproducibility, but these documentation regressions are outweighed by the improved controls and evidence.
